Two public-sector customers require an updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy. ## High-Level Requirements | ID | Priority | Requirement | |-------|----------|-------------| | HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. | | HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. | | HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. | ## Affected Components - Dashboard - Documentation ## Out of Scope - Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require - Flows outside the four audited ones ## Open Questions None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow. After this epic, each flow is fully operable by keyboard alone, with no focus traps, no unreachable controls, and consistent visible focus indicators. ## Scope - Attach the accessibility audit report (the per-flow defect enumeration) to this epic before implementation starts; it is the authoritative defect list for the verification AC below. - Fix every keyboard-accessibility defect enumerated in the audit report for the four audited flows (focus loss in modals, unreachable controls, inconsistent focus indicators). - Ensure end-to-end keyboard-only operability for each of the four flows: project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission. - Make focus indicators consistent across all controls within the audited flows. ## Audit Defect List The audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow. Per the strategy, the defect classes found across the four audited flows are: 1. Focus lost or trapped in modals/dialogs. 2. Controls unreachable via keyboard. 3. Inconsistent (or missing) visible focus indicators. The attached audit report is the authoritative enumeration; the classes above are the summary derived from the strategy and must reconcile with it when the report is attached. Out of scope (per strategy): - Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require. - Flows outside the four audited ones. ## Acceptance Criteria - Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end to end using keyboard alone. - No focus traps: focus never becomes stuck or lost in modals or dialogs within the audited flows. - Every control in the audited flows is reachable and operable via keyboard. - Focus indicators are visible and consistent across all controls in the audited flows. - The accessibility audit report is attached to this epic, and its per-flow defect enumeration reconciles with the Audit Defect List section above (modal focus loss, unreachable controls, inconsistent focus indicators). - Every defect enumerated in the attached audit report for these flows is verified fixed, with each defect checked off against the report's enumeration. ## HLR Traceability - HLR-1 (P1): the four audited core flows fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls — fully covered. - HLR-2 (P1): visible focus indicators consistent across the audited flows — fully covered. Not docs-only: Dashboard requires code changes. Full decomposition (Steps 1-8) was executed. ## Epic List | ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority | |----|-------|------|------|----------| | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility fixes for core Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 | | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 | ## Dependency DAG ```mermaid graph TD E001["RHAISTRAT-9017-E001

Focus-indicator consistency is part of the same keyboard-operability remediation and shares the same UI surfaces — splitting would duplicate work and create artificial boundaries (Step 4 / Rule 1). The strategy states open questions are none — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow, so remediation scope is fully specified and no unknown changes which epics exist or what they do. ## Tiered Delivery Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing. ## Health Warnings - **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): Affected Components is a bare list (no per-component change/owner detail), and there is no Impacted Teams table, Dependencies table, Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, or Non-Functional Requirements section. Epic acceptance criteria were derived from the HLRs and problem statement. - **Team assumption**: the Documentation owner is not specified anywhere in the strategy; `RHOAI Documentation` was assumed for E002 and should be verified before scheduling. - **Priority observation** (non-blocking): the problem statement says two public-sector customers require a republished VPAT before renewal, yet HLR-3 and the strategy priority are P2/Normal. Epic Boundaries (2/2) Different component/team tuples produce separate epics: E001 (Dashboard / RHOAI Dashboard, code) and E002 (Documentation / RHOAI Documentation, content). Work-product type boundary correctly applied — code implementation and substantive conformance-content authoring are separate epics per Step 5 Rule 1. No scope duplication between the epics (E001 remediates code; E002 documents the result). E001's scope (audit-enumerated defects across four flows, with the audit report as the authoritative defect list) is plausibly a single sprint's work; no oversized epic detected. ### 4. Type Correctness (2/2) Both epics are Implementation and produce concrete artifacts (fixed Dashboard code; republished VPAT and accessibility statement). E002 correctly carries `implementation_type: docs-authoring`. No Investigation epics — correctly so: the strategy states open questions are none and the audit enumerates the exact defects, so no unknown changes which epics exist or what they do. `gated_by` is null on both epics with no Investigation dependencies, so no gating metadata issues. ### 5. AI Implementability Scoring (2/2) Both epics are Implementation and correctly carry `ai_signals` (9-signal rubric); `investigation_signals` is null as expected. Both `-ai-signals.md` rationale files exist and their values match the frontmatter. E001: values are consistent with the rubric and strategy (change_specificity +1 justified by the per-flow audit enumeration; open_questions +1 matches the strategy's "None"; repo_access +1 matches the public odh-dashboard repo per architecture context; pattern_precedent 0 neutral is fair given no evidenced prior a11y remediation; architecture_claims 0 correct since the strategy cites no architecture context). No signal contradicts the rubric conditions. (Arithmetic/thresholds not checked, per instructions.) ### 6. Acceptance Criteria Quality (2/2) E001 has testable ACs derived from the HLRs: per-flow end-to-end keyboard operability, no focus traps, all controls reachable, consistent focus indicators, plus audit-report attachment and per-defect verification reconciliation. E002 has testable ACs including the Rule 24-mandated "technically reviewed against the implemented fixes" AC and a no-overstatement clause scoping claims to the implemented fixes. Rule 23 (rollback/feature-flag) does not apply — no capability replacement. Rule 25 (build pipeline green) does not apply — no konflux-onboarding in any dependency chain. No sibling-epic draft-ID references in either epic body. ### 7. Completeness (2/2) All strategy scope is covered: keyboard operability of the four audited flows (E001), consistent focus indicators (E001), VPAT and accessibility statement updated/republished with technical review (E002). Out-of-scope items (screen-reader semantics beyond keyboard fixes, other flows) are honored in both epics. No conditional branches to verify. The strategy's problem-statement driver — two public-sector customers requiring a republished VPAT before renewal — is surfaced in the decomposition summary's health warnings (priority observation) rather than silently dropped, though it would be stronger carried into E002's body as stakeholder context (minor, below). The docs-authoring epic is present as HLR-3 requires. The Documentation-team assumption and missing strategy sections are properly logged as health warnings rather than silently papered over.
